Our company is launching a wellness program and I have been asked to coordinate the cafeteria lunch menu for the upcoming week. There is a corporate nutrition guidelines page available at http://localhost:30206/guidelines.html that outlines the daily nutritional intake targets for a healthy adult, including recommended calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrate amounts per meal, along with notes about common dietary restrictions our employees have reported such as vegetarian and low-sodium preferences.

Please start by visiting that guidelines page and extracting all the nutritional targets and dietary notes listed there. The page has a table with per-meal targets for lunch specifically, and a section listing the top dietary restrictions reported by employees.

Next, search the recipe database for Chinese dishes that would be suitable for a corporate cafeteria lunch. I need you to find at least two main dishes from the meat category, at least two dishes from the vegetable category, and at least one soup or staple dish. For each dish, note the name, category, and any available ingredient or preparation details.

Once you have the recipes, create a Google Sheets spreadsheet called "Wellness_Lunch_Menu" with a sheet named "Weekly_Plan". This sheet should have columns for Day (Monday through Friday), Main_Dish_1, Main_Dish_2, Side_Dish, Soup_Or_Staple, Estimated_Calories, Estimated_Protein_g, Estimated_Fat_g, and Estimated_Carbs_g. Assign the recipes you found across the five days, reusing dishes if needed but trying to vary the menu. Fill in estimated nutritional values per meal based on reasonable estimates for Chinese dishes, keeping them within the guidelines you found on the website. Add a second sheet called "Nutrition_Summary" with columns for Nutrient, Daily_Target, Menu_Average, and Within_Target (Yes or No), with rows for Calories, Protein, Fat, and Carbs.

After the spreadsheet is ready, write a Word document called Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx in the workspace. This document should have a title "Corporate Wellness Lunch Program", a brief introduction explaining the program goals, a section listing the five daily menus with dish names, and a section summarizing how the menu aligns with the nutritional guidelines. Mention any dishes that accommodate dietary restrictions.

Finally, send an email from wellness@company.com to cafeteria-manager@company.com with the subject "Weekly Wellness Lunch Menu - March 2026" that provides an overview of the meal plan, highlights the nutritional targets from the guidelines, and lists all the dishes selected for the week.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, run the four independent read-only sources in one wave and keep their complete page/category responses out of the main context. The recipe categories can exceed the model-output limit, so their owners must be explore sub-agents constrained to read-only source work; they may read the runtime `output_path` but must not write a deliverable or mutate any external system.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 4 explore sub-agents as parallel individual Agent calls:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to read the complete nutrition-guidelines page at `http://localhost:30206/guidelines.html` with read-only browser operations. Return the exact lunch targets for calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrates, every reported dietary restriction/note, and page/table/field controls.
   2. explore 1 (web-domain-researcher 1): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact recipe category `荤菜`. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime `output_path`, read that file from the task workspace instead of retrying the category call. Select at least two distinct cafeteria-suitable recipe IDs, retrieve only those exact IDs in native parallel, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], category:"荤菜", category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.
   3. explore 2 (web-domain-researcher 2): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact recipe category `素菜`. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime `output_path`, read that file from the task workspace instead of retrying the category call. Select at least two distinct cafeteria-suitable recipe IDs, retrieve only those exact IDs in native parallel, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], category:"素菜", category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.
   4. explore 3 (web-domain-researcher 3): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact category `汤`; only when that returned collection has no usable recipe may it query exact category `主食`. Consume any overlong runtime `output_path` from the task workspace without repeating the call, select at least one suitable exact recipe ID, retrieve only that ID, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], requested_category:"汤", used_category, fallback_reason, category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.

After Wave 1, the main agent must require at least two meat, two vegetable, and one soup/staple recipe with unique exact IDs, freeze an explicit Monday-Friday menu (reusing only those verified dishes when needed), and derive reasonable meal-level estimates that remain consistent with the source targets. Freeze the task-visible agent-workspace absolute path from the Visible Boundary/current working directory; never assume `/workspace`. From that frozen menu, dispatch the three independent output branches in the same response: (1) coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): own exactly one `Wellness_Lunch_Menu` spreadsheet with `Weekly_Plan` and `Nutrition_Summary` using the task's exact columns/rows; (2) coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): own `<agent_workspace>/Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx` with the exact title, five daily menus, guideline alignment, and supported dietary accommodations; and (3) coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): send exactly one message from `wellness@company.com` to `cafeteria-manager@company.com` with subject `Weekly Wellness Lunch Menu - March 2026`. Read both artifacts once in native-parallel calls, then reconcile dish names, targets, estimates, averages, Within_Target decisions, and email content. Do not dispatch a verification agent.

You are researching a Chinese recipe database to select dishes for a corporate cafeteria wellness lunch menu (March 10-14, 2026).

## Context
Our company wellness program needs a balanced 5-day Chinese lunch menu. Corporate nutrition guidelines require:
- At least 2 meat dishes (category 荤菜), including at least one chicken or beef option
- At least 2 vegetable dishes (category 素菜), must be fully vegetarian
- At least 1 soup (category 汤), light broth-based preferred
- At least 1 staple (category 主食), rice/noodle
- Dietary restrictions to accommodate: vegetarian (23% of employees), low-sodium (18%), gluten-free (12%), no-pork (15% - pork dishes must be labeled)

## Tools available to you
- `mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById` — query a recipe by Chinese name or ID (fuzzy match). ONE query per call.
- `mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory` — list recipes by category. Categories: 水产, 早餐, 调料, 甜品, 饮品, 荤菜, 半成品加工, 汤, 主食, 素菜

## IMPORTANT constraints
- Do NOT call `mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getAllRecipes` (output is enormous).
- AVOID `getRecipesByCategory` for 荤菜 or 素菜 — those return 100,000+ characters and will overflow your context. Prefer targeted `getRecipeById` lookups by dish name.
- You MAY use `getRecipesByCategory` for 汤 and 主食 only if needed (smaller categories), but prefer `getRecipeById` first.

## Dishes to look up (use getRecipeById with these Chinese names; if a name returns no match, note it and try a close alternative)
1. 荤菜 (meat): 土豆炖牛肉 — OR 萝卜炖牛肉
2. 荤菜 (meat): 红烧鸡翅 — OR 可乐鸡翅
3. 素菜 (vegetable): 地三鲜
4. 素菜 (vegetable): 蒜蓉西兰花 — OR 清炒西兰花
5. 素菜 (vegetable, alternate): 麻婆豆腐
6. 汤 (soup): 番茄蛋汤 — OR 紫菜蛋花汤
7. 主食 (staple): 扬州炒饭

I already have details for 宫保鸡丁 (Kung Pao Chicken, 荤菜, chicken thigh + scallion + dried chili + peanut + soy sauce/vinegar/sugar stir-fry), so do NOT re-query that one.

## Deliverable
Return a COMPACT markdown summary (not raw JSON, not full step lists). For EACH dish you successfully found, provide:
- **Name** (Chinese, plus a short English translation)
- **Category** (荤菜 / 素菜 / 汤 / 主食)
- **Key ingredients** (top 5-8, with amounts if given)
- **Preparation summary** (1-2 sentences describing the cooking method)
- **Difficulty** (if listed)
- **Dietary notes**: vegetarian? gluten-free? contains pork? sodium level (high/medium/low based on soy sauce/salt usage)

Also state clearly which dishes could NOT be found in the database and what alternatives you found instead.

Keep your final report under 1500 words. Do not dump full ingredient lists or full step arrays.
Research Chinese recipes for menu

## Tools
- `mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById` — query by Chinese dish name (fuzzy match), one per call.
- Do NOT call `getAllRecipes`, and do NOT use `getRecipesByCategory` for 荤菜 or 素菜 (output too large).

## Dishes to look up (use these exact Chinese names; if one is not found, note it and try one close alternative)
**Meat dishes (荤菜):**

2. 葱爆羊肉

**Soups (汤):**

## Deliverable
For EACH dish successfully found, give me a COMPACT summary (no raw JSON, no full step arrays):
- **Name** (Chinese + short English translation)
- **Category** (荤菜 / 汤 / etc.)
- **Key ingredients** (top 5-8)
- **Preparation summary** (1 sentence)
- **Difficulty**
- **Dietary notes**: vegetarian? gluten-free? contains pork? sodium level (low/medium/high based on soy sauce/salt/processed ingredients)

Also explicitly list any dishes that were NOT found in the database and what you substituted.

Keep the final report under 1200 words. Be concise and factual — I only need enough to describe each dish in a menu and estimate its nutrition.
Find more meat dishes and soups

## Document specification

**Document title (Heading 1, first line):** Corporate Wellness Lunch Program

### Section 1 — Heading 1: "Program Introduction"
Paragraphs (plain body text):
1. "The Corporate Wellness Lunch Program provides balanced, freshly prepared Chinese cuisine in the company cafeteria for the week of March 10 - March 14, 2026 (Monday through Friday). All dishes are sourced from our approved Chinese recipe database and are served as single cafeteria portions."
2. "The goals of the program are: (1) supply steady energy and concentration through the working day; (2) deliver balanced macronutrition that meets the corporate nutrition targets established by the wellness committee with registered dietitians; (3) accommodate the dietary restrictions reported in the Q4 2025 employee survey; and (4) offer genuine variety so employees look forward to lunch every day."
3. "Every lunch follows the required meal composition: at least one main protein dish supplying 15 g or more of protein per serving, at least one vegetable dish, and one soup or rice/noodle staple. On the three soup days a standard 100 g portion of steamed rice is also served so that carbohydrate targets are met."

### Section 2 — Heading 1: "Nutritional Guidelines Targets (Per Lunch)"

- Thursday | Sweet & Sour Pork Tenderloin (糖醋里脊) | Green Beans with Minced Pork & Preserved Olives (榄菜肉末四季豆) | Garlic Broccoli (蒜蓉西兰花) | Enoki Mushroom Soup (金针菇汤)
- Friday | Yu-Xiang Shredded Pork (鱼香肉丝) | Mapo Tofu (麻婆豆腐) | Stir-Fried Leafy Greens (炒青菜) | Scallion Oil Noodles (葱油拌面)

Day | Calories (kcal) | Protein (g) | Fat (g) | Carbs (g)
- Monday | 670 | 32 | 20 | 72
- Tuesday | 680 | 32 | 23 | 86
- Wednesday | 690 | 33 | 21 | 73

1. "Menu averages compare favourably with the daily targets: 684 kcal against a 650 kcal target (acceptable range 500-800), 32.6 g protein against 30 g (range 20-45), 22.8 g fat against 22 g (range 15-30), and 75.8 g carbohydrates against 80 g (range 55-110). Every single day also falls inside the acceptable range for all four nutrients, so no day requires correction."
2. "Meal composition requirements are met on every day: each day's Main Dish 1 supplies well over 15 g of protein per serving (17 g to 19 g), each day includes at least one vegetable dish, and each day closes with either a light broth soup or a rice/noodle staple."
3. "The variety requirement is satisfied: eighteen different dishes appear across the twenty meal slots, and only two dishes repeat — Garlic Broccoli (蒜蓉西兰花) and Stir-Fried Leafy Greens (炒青菜), each appearing twice."

### Section 5 — Heading 1: "Dietary Restriction Accommodations"
Intro paragraph: "The Q4 2025 employee survey (847 respondents) identified four priority restrictions. Each is addressed below."

Heading 2: "Vegetarian (23% of respondents)"
Paragraph: "Every day offers at least one fully vegetarian dish. Monday: Tomato & Scrambled Egg and Seaweed & Egg Drop Soup. Tuesday: Hot & Sour Shredded Potato and Stir-Fried Leafy Greens. Wednesday: Sautéed Potato, Eggplant & Pepper (地三鲜). Thursday: Enoki Mushroom Soup. Friday: Stir-Fried Leafy Greens and Scallion Oil Noodles. The kitchen should swap the oyster sauce in Garlic Broccoli and Smashed Cucumber Salad for a mushroom-based vegetarian alternative so those sides are fully vegetarian as well."

Heading 2: "Low-Sodium (18% of respondents)"
Paragraph: "The three soups — Seaweed & Egg Drop Soup, Clear Lamb Soup and Enoki Mushroom Soup — are light, broth-based and naturally low in sodium. Added salt and soy sauce should be reduced by roughly one third in Sweet & Sour Pork Tenderloin, Yu-Xiang Shredded Pork, Mapo Tofu, Green Beans with Minced Pork & Preserved Olives and Yangzhou Fried Rice, and MSG should be omitted."

Heading 2: "Gluten-Free (12% of respondents)"
Paragraph: "At least one gluten-free option is available daily: Monday — Seaweed & Egg Drop Soup; Tuesday — Stir-Fried Leafy Greens and Yangzhou Fried Rice; Wednesday — Clear Lamb Soup; Thursday — Enoki Mushroom Soup; Friday — Stir-Fried Leafy Greens. Steamed rice is naturally gluten-free, and gluten-free tamari can replace soy sauce to widen the choice further."

Heading 2: "No Pork (15% of respondents)"
Paragraph: "Pork-containing dishes must be clearly labelled at the serving line: Tuesday — Yangzhou Fried Rice (canned luncheon meat); Thursday — Sweet & Sour Pork Tenderloin and Green Beans with Minced Pork & Preserved Olives; Friday — Yu-Xiang Shredded Pork and Mapo Tofu. Monday and Wednesday are entirely pork-free, and a plain steamed rice option should be offered alongside the fried rice."

Paragraph: "The full five-day plan and the nutrient summary are maintained in the Google Sheets workbook 'Wellness_Lunch_Menu' (sheets 'Weekly_Plan' and 'Nutrition_Summary'). The cafeteria team should confirm portion sizes and the salt reductions above, and the wellness committee will review actual take-up after the first week of service."

- Set document title metadata to "Corporate Wellness Lunch Program" when creating the document.
- Save exactly as Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx in the workspace directory given above.

## Deliverable
